narrative.overview:
The site is one version history. Stephen's career and products read as releases of a single product, newest on top: the latest release (who he is now, with an Assets panel beside it), then a dated rail of earlier releases back to 2016, a ruled Skills list and an inverted contact band. Its vocabulary is changelog grammar on a cool paper ground: calendar version tags, coloured change labels, dated entries with live nodes, shortstat counts and an assets list. It refuses the hero-plus-project-cards portfolio.

The page is text-first and ruled, at the density of a good release page: 1px rules, measured line lengths, and colour that carries meaning rather than decoration. Cobalt is the only action colour; green, blue and amber are change meaning. Pictorial colour appears in exactly two places, the covers of the two featured releases, each in its own product's identity: SiapKnow's own site, as a screenshot on SiapKnow's field, and Myrna & Judith's leaf field with fanned App Store screenshots.

It is static and script-free. Light and dark both follow prefers-color-scheme, with no toggle, and motion is two CSS moments, both off under reduced motion: the Latest badge stamps in once, and rail nodes light as their release scrolls in. The 404 and redirect pages reuse site.css; the Writerside archive pages keep their own look and sit outside this system.
keyCharacteristics: One release history, newest first; work enters as an entry on the rail, never as a card grid.
Changelog devices are the whole vocabulary: calendar tags, a dated rail with live nodes, change labels, shortstat lines, an assets panel.
Cool paper, navy ink and one cobalt action colour; status hues only where they mean something.
Flat and ruled: 1px rules, tonal tints and an inverted band instead of elevation.
Product colour lives only inside the two featured covers.
Both colour schemes follow the system; there is no JavaScript.

rules.name: The Meaning Rule
rules.body: Green, changed-blue and amber appear only as change meaning: green for what was added, shipped or is live; blue for what changed, was led or is current; amber only for what is in progress. A rail node turns green only when its entry carries a live status.

rules.name: The Cover Rule
rules.body: The sk-* and mj-* tokens never leave their covers. Outside them, a product appears only through its own icon or mark (44px entry icons, 22px inline marks).

rules.name: The Tint Rule
rules.body: Hover fills, tile fills and outlines are color-mix(in srgb, <token> N%, transparent) tints of an existing token, never new colours: ink at 5% (row hover) and 7% (icon tile); action at 9% (the resume row, outlined-link hover), 15% (resume row hover) and 45% (outlined-link border); added and progress at 35% (status borders); added at 40% (the Latest ring). On the band, the ghost border mixes band-ink 40% into band.

rules.name: The Six-Hundred Rule
rules.body: Every Inter Tight heading, from the 6rem name to the 16px panel title, is 600. Heavier weights belong to small text that has to hold at size: 650 for buttons and asset names, 700 for labels, badges and bold text, 720 for skill group names. Only the Manrope name reaches 800.

rules.name: The Tight-at-Size Rule
rules.body: Tracking tightens as size grows: -0.04em on display and headlines, -0.035em on years and the name, -0.03em on entry titles, -0.02em on the subhead and the contact email, -0.01em on the Assets title and entry roles. Body text keeps normal tracking.

rules.name: The Metadata Mono Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono sets only release metadata: calendar tags, entry date ranges, file names and handles in the Assets list, sizes, and shortstat counts. It never sets prose, headings, labels or buttons. Year labels and the hero's "Updated" date stay in Inter Tight.

rules.name: The Rail Alignment Rule
rules.body: From 960px the history and skills content starts at the rail offset, calc(var(--rail) + 32px): the Version history head, the Skills heading and the skills list all line up with the entries column, not the page edge.

rules.name: The Flat Release Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat; separation comes from 1px rules, tonal tints and inverted fields. The only cast shadow belongs to the product screenshots inside the Myrna & Judith cover.

rules.name: The Label-Versus-State Rule
rules.body: Change labels and calendar tags are 6px rectangles; kind and status chips are pills. "Shipped" (a change) and "Live on iOS and Android" (a state) share a colour, so shape tells them apart.

dos: Do add new work as an entry in its year: entry tag, a mono date range if it spans time, kind chip, status, then change lines that each open with one coloured verb.
Do pick label colours by meaning: Shipped Green for New, Added and Shipped; Changed Blue for Changed, Updated, Improved, Built, Led, Maintained and Current; Progress Amber only for In progress.
Do date every count: shortstat lines end with "Counted <date>", and star counts carry their month.
Do define every new colour twice, in :root and in the prefers-color-scheme: dark block.
Do derive hovers, tile fills and outlines from existing tokens with color-mix (5 to 15% fills, 35 to 45% borders).
Do keep keyframe animation and smooth scrolling behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, on --ease-out, in CSS only.
donts: Don't present work as a hero with project cards or a card grid; it enters the history as a release.
Don't set prose, headings, labels or buttons in JetBrains Mono.
Don't use the sk-* or mj-* tokens outside their covers.
Don't give page surfaces drop shadows; borders may be 1px inset rings, and the only cast shadow is the screenshot lift inside the Myrna & Judith cover.
Don't set Inter Tight headings above 600, or use Manrope for anything but the header name.
Don't make a status chip or rail node green for anything that isn't live now; green chips mean live, running or current.
Don't add a theme toggle or any JavaScript; both schemes follow prefers-color-scheme, and the home page's CSP sets script-src 'none'.
